jd_text:
Who We Are
FTI Consulting is the leading global expert firm for organizations facing crisis and transformation. We work with many of the world’s top multinational corporations, law firms, banks and private equity firms on their most important issues to deliver impact that makes a difference. From resolving disputes, navigating crises, managing risk and optimizing performance, our teams respond rapidly to dynamic and complex situations.
At FTI Consulting, you’ll work side-by side with leaders who have shaped history, helping solve the biggest challenges making headlines today. From day one, you’ll be an integral part of a focused team where you can make a real impact. You’ll be surrounded by an open, collaborative culture that embraces diversity, recognition, professional development and, most importantly, you.
Are you ready to make your impact?
About The Role 
In Business Transformation at FTI Consulting, we focus on our clients’ strategic, operational, financial and capital needs by addressing the full spectrum of financial and transactional challenges faced by corporations, boards, private equity sponsors, creditor constituencies and other stakeholders. Our services include pre-deal commercial and operations due diligence, post-merger integration, business plan development, restructuring and performance improvement including interim management. Our demanding customer base relies on small and senior teams.
What You’ll Do
The successful candidate will participate in project teams, working with clients on the execution of various engagements and assist with ongoing business development activity.
As such, key activities include:
- Modelling financial and operational scenarios
- Analysing operations (e.g. OEE assessment, FTE benchmarking)
- Assessing company financials
- Researching markets
- Formulating strategy
- Developing business plans
- Identifying upside / downside potential
- Creating implementable improvement plans
- Planning carve-outs and integrations
- Conducting private equity due diligence
- Managing and implementing programmes
- Writing presentations and reports
- Attending client/internal meetings (including regular and extensive travel)
- Supporting junior team members
How You’ll Grow 
We are committed to investing and supporting you in your professional development and we have developed a range of programs focused on fostering leadership, growth and development opportunities. We aim to promote continuous learning and individual skills development through on-the-job learning, self-guided professional development courses and certifications. You’ll be assigned a dedicated coach to mentor, guide and support you through regular coaching sessions and serve as an advocate for your professional growth. 
As you progress through your career at FTI Consulting, we offer tailored programs for critical professional milestones to ensure you are prepared and empowered to take on your next role.
What You Will Need to Succeed 
Basic Qualifications
- University degree level (or equivalent), preferably in a numerical degree or that has a numerical element
- Demonstrable consulting experience.
- Project experience in high paced environments focused on rapid results (e.g. rapid performance improvement, turnaround, due diligence)
- Work experience and the ability to demonstrate results delivery across functions in at least some of the following focus areas:
- Performance improvement, ideally turnaround, including diagnosis
- Operations
- Financial modelling
- Business plan review/development
- Industry experience (e.g. consumer goods, retail, pharma, transportation and logistics, travel and leisure)
- Implementation
- Programme management
- Strategy
- Market assessment
- Transactions experience 
Preferred Qualifications 
- Additional industry experience an advantage
- Excellent consulting skills, specifically:
- Proven ability to take a hypothesis focused approach to solve problems from first principals
- Strong verbal communication skills and the ability to interact with team members and clients at all levels using a range of styles to suit the audience
- Strong written communication skills with experience of producing / leading production of client ready PowerPoint documents for senior audiences
- Relationship building skills, with the ability to quickly build rapport, develop strong working relationships and work in diverse teams
- Excellent organizational and planning skills and confident working with a number of demanding stakeholders, with the ability to handle multiple tasks
- Equally strong EQ and IQ
- Excel based analytic and modelling skills
- Good knowledge of P&L, cash flow and balance sheet
- Demonstrable and relevant industry expertise in companies with complex operations or environments highly preferred
- Fluent Spanish speaker and writer

Are you ready to make your impact?
About The Role 
Within the Corporate Finance practice, our Power, Renewables & Energy Transition team is a leading adviser to businesses, lenders, equity and infrastructure investors, law firms, and utilities in the US, UK, Europe and internationally. We have been involved in a wide range of engagements drawing on our finance, accounting, economic, and industry expertise. We provide critical insight and advisory support in the context of strategic decision-making, financial and operational restructuring, due diligence, transaction advisory, merger integration, lender advisory, business carve-outs and performance improvement. The sectors we work in span the energy industry and include solar, wind, energy storage, e-mobility, utilities, thermal generation, advanced nuclear, and hydrogen, amongst others.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
What You Will Do 
Senior Consultants are centrally involved in preparing and managing financial analysis and models and formal written reports and presentations. They are expected to be able to take responsibility for research and other gathering of information, managing and carrying out quantitative, industry and market analysis and report their findings in a clear, concise, and structured way, both internally and to clients. Senior Consultants may be responsible for managing the output of more junior colleagues and liaising with clients as necessary. Ideal candidates will be problem-solvers who enjoy developing approaches to solve complex, unstructured problems in a logical manner. 
How You Will Grow  
We are committed to investing and supporting you in your professional development and we have developed a range of programs focused on fostering leadership, growth and development opportunities. We aim to promote continuous learning and individual skills development through on-the-job learning, self-guided professional development courses and certifications. You will be assigned a dedicated coach to mentor, guide and support you through regular coaching sessions and serve as an advocate for your professional growth.   
As you progress through your career at FTI Consulting, we offer tailored programs for critical professional milestones to ensure you are prepared and empowered to take on your next role. 
What You Will Need To Succeed
Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Finance, Accounting, or any related business field
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant post-graduate professional experience
- Ability to travel to clients and to FTI offices as needed
Preferred Qualifications 
- Meaningful experience in financial statement analysis and financial modelling (e.g., 3-statement, 13-week cash flow, DCF, etc.)
- Effective in communicating orally and in writing, including experience writing formal reports and presentations 
- Ability to work independently in fast-paced, multi-task environment

We Do Consulting Differently
We Do Consulting Differently
BRG is launching a new capital markets group within its Financial Institutions Advisory practice that will focus on helping financial institutions, including broker-dealers, investment advisers, swap dealers, and other capital market participants, solve pressing business, regulatory, and compliance issues. The group includes former regulators, compliance experts, financial modelers, technologists, and former industry professionals, that advise clients with immediate risks to drive tangible benefits.
BRG is currently seeking a Consultant or Managing Consultant to support and oversee engagement workstreams across a range of complex regulatory compliance, risk management, and client advisory projects within the capital markets sector. This is an opportunity to help build a new practice within an established consulting firm. We are looking for professionals who are eager to build on their experience working in the financial services industry and who enjoy using their analytical ability and strong organizational skills to solve complex problems, working directly with clients, and helping to build a growing business.
Responsibilities:
Consultant / Managing Consultant
- Work directly with senior professionals to execute financial institution advisory projects related to regulatory compliance and risk management. Functional areas of work include supervision, governance, technology and operations enablement, and business process optimization.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of frameworks and methodologies for compliance, supervisory, operational, and regulatory risk management programs.
- Assess client policies, procedures, and controls against leading practices and industry frameworks. Identify gaps in design and execution, and present actionable recommendations.
- Plan and execute assigned project tasks and support project administration and day-to-day client communications. Prioritize assignments and responsibilities to meet engagement goals and deadlines. 
- Apply creative problem-solving and relevant software tools, analytical methods, and computer models to develop client solutions efficiently. Prepare client deliverables and contribute to expert reports. Present findings and recommendations in coordination with engagement leads.
- Participate in practice meetings, business development initiatives, and office activities, including staff training and recruiting. 
- Additional Managing Consultant Responsibilities
- Lead the development and implementation of risk-management frameworks and methodologies within assigned engagements or workstreams. 
- Plan and manage client engagements or assigned workstreams, depending on engagement size and complexity. Responsibilities include project administration, contracting, budget management, and day-to-day client relationships.
- Manage project work by delegating assignments, guiding staff, monitoring progress, and prioritizing work to meet goals and deadlines. Prepare and review deliverables for completeness and accuracy, oversee contributions to expert reports, and present findings and recommendations to client management.
- Lead assigned business development activities, including proposal preparation and prospective-client presentations, and take an active role in staff training and recruiting.
Qualifications 
Consultant / Managing Consultant
- Minimum four (4) years of relevant experience in regulatory compliance, supervision, or risk management within a financial institution, regulatory agency, or consulting firm. Preferred focus on broker-dealers, investment advisers, asset or wealth management firms, swap dealers, or other capital markets businesses. 
- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university, or equivalent work experience.
- Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, and the ability to prepare clear analyses and presentations.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills, desire to work within a team environment, and ability to manage processes and other more junior staff, as necessary.
- Ability to travel to client sites as needed.
Additional Managing Consultant Qualifications:
- Minimum of six (6) years of direct experience assessing or advising on compliance with applicable SEC, FINRA, CFTC, NFA, or state regulatory requirements and expectations, with a strong preference for candidates who have worked in a regulatory agency’s enforcement or examinations division. 
- Demonstrated experience conducting risk and control assessments, developing process maps and workflows, assessing compliance with capital markets regulations, and conducting markets compliance testing and financial harm analysis. 
- Proven project or program management experience, including planning and coordinating work, guiding staff, reviewing deliverables, and managing client communications.
Consultant Salary Range: $115,000 – $145,000
Managing Consultant: $145,000 – $190,000
Job title and compensation to be determined based on qualifications and experience.   
Candidate must be able to submit verification of his/her legal right to work in the U.S., without company sponsorship. 
About BRG
BRG combines world-leading academic credentials with world-tested business expertise and purpose-built emerging technologies. Our culture centers on agility and connectivity which sets us apart and gets you ahead.  
At BRG, our professionals include specialist consultants, industry experts, renowned academics, and leading-edge data scientists. Together, they bring a diversity of real-world experience, data, and human and artificial intelligence, to economics, disputes, and investigations; corporate finance; and performance improvement services that address the most complex challenges facing organizations across the globe.
Our unique structure nurtures the interdisciplinary relationships that give us the edge, laying the groundwork for more informed insights and more original, incisive thinking.  When paired with our global reach and resources, our diverse perspectives and technical capabilities make us uniquely capable to address our clients’ challenges. We get results because we know how to apply our thinking to your world.
At BRG, we don’t just show you what’s possible. We’re built to help you make it happen. 
BRG is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. As a Senior Consultant, you will be a mentor, trainer, and coach to Interns and Consultants as you facilitate the successful completion of project work plans. You’ll identify areas of risk and opportunities to increase efficiency. You’ll strengthen relationships and deepen your abilities to communicate, gain trust, and network with client personnel and professional associates.  At the direction of Managers, you may accept responsibility for decision-making in areas including establishing project scope and work plans, project staffing, preparation of deliverables, and application of methodologies.

- You enjoy identifying areas of opportunity to improve the efficiency and profitability of the client’s overall business processes.

- Process improvement, business transformation, finance transformation, and project management methodologies  
- Accounting / finance processes and objectives  
- Accounting operations, financial frameworks, financial accounting systems and business intelligence tools  
- Process analysis and assessments as well as development of process flows and future state roadmaps  
- Service excellence - identifying key client business issues, determining client needs by supplementing the standard assessment techniques and tools with innovative approaches, evaluating and validating analysis and developing recommendations for the client in the context of the overall engagement

Protiviti practices a hybrid model, which is a combination of working in person with a purpose and working remotely. This model creates meaningful experiences for our people and our clients while offering a flexible environment. The ratio of remote to in-person requirements vary by client, project, team, and other business factors. title: Consultant – Energy Providers
summary:

Support Federal clients across the full spectrum of financial management, including federal grants, reimbursable agreements, procurement processes, and budget formulation and execution. Financial Management & Analysis:
- Provide ongoing financial management support to Federal clients in accordance with applicable Federal financial management requirements and guidance.
- Support the quantitative development of business case documentation (for example, needs analyses and cost/benefit analyses).
- Prepare, review, and reconcile financial documents such as federal financial transaction data, reimbursable agreements, and grant related financial records.
- Identify opportunities for process improvement and propose practical recommendations to enhance financial operations and controls.
Client Delivery & Communication:
- Develop clear, well-structured deliverables (presentations, reports, analyses, dashboards) that synthesize complex financial information into actionable insights and recommendations for clients, including visually appealing, high-level summaries of large financial datasets for various levels of stakeholders.
- Facilitate client meetings and working sessions to gather data, understand requirements, and validate findings.
- Communicate with client and internal stakeholders on project status, findings, and next steps, including explaining financial concepts to non-financial audiences and summarizing key takeaways from external and internal stakeholder meetings.
- Provide analysis and insight to managers and leadership to inform decision-making and project direction.

- Perform research and analysis to identify and obtain needed information, including applicable Federal regulations, policies, best practices, and public financial data sources such as USASpending.gov to investigate financial transaction-level discrepancies.

- Recommend changes to processes, tools, or documentation to solve problems and improve efficiency or compliance, including documenting current data analysis processes, identifying improvement opportunities, and iterating on data displays or communication methods to advance PMO goals.

jd_text:
About the team
We are looking for social researchers/public policy consultants to join a well-established practice within ICF that develops, analyses and evaluates UK Government policies and programmes across priority social policy domains, including education/employment, communities, youth and families. ICF’s clients include government departments and agencies such as the Department for Education, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government and the Department for Work and Pensions – as well as local government and leading charities. From day one, you will have the opportunity to contribute to a varied range of influential research projects across the UK. We are particularly interested in hearing from people with a background or interest in sport and active leisure, as well as broader social policy topics such as youth inclusion and employment.
Your main responsibilities will be to:
- Perform research and analysis on public policy issues and programmes for public and third sector clients, by:
- Carrying out research and analysing / summarising academic and policy literature.
- Conducting face to face, telephone and video interviews, writing up interviews and focus groups, and carrying out qualitative analysis using a variety of tools and software.
- Analysing quantitative data using a variety of tools and software.
- Generating insightful findings, preparing descriptive and analytical texts and data visualisations.
- Providing research and administrative support to other team members.
Essential Requirements:
- Qualifications relevant to social policy or research methods (graduate or postgraduate, for example but not limited to social sciences, economics or health economics, applied statistics, geography, political science, service design, psychology or sociology, public policy research or public administration).
-  1-2 years’ employment experience of using a variety of methods (qualitative and/or quantitative) in research projects (either own project and/or as part of a team) for analyst roles, and 3+ years’ experience for consultant roles.
- Strong interest in UK policy, the improvement of public services and use of evidence in policy making.
- Excellent oral and written English.
- Excellent time management skills.
- Intermediate or advanced computer user skills related to carrying out research and data analysis.
Desirable:
- Skills in editing or proofreading other people’s written work.
- Experience in undertaking evaluations of projects or programmes.
- Knowledge of the work of UK government departments.
Personal Qualities:
- Ability to write skilfully and accurately summarise and synthesise information and evidence from a wide range of sources.
- Highly developed interpersonal / communication skills, and ability to work with a multidisciplinary team spread across the UK.
- Sound research and business ethics.
- Ability to manage own time and be flexible to handle multiple priorities, managing a varied workload to meet deadlines.
- High level of attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong, demonstrable commitment to helping us build an inclusive team that values diversity.
Ready to apply?
We are recruiting into our London, Birmingham and Plymouth offices. Please state your preference in your covering letter. We have a hybrid working model that supports our employees to work from a base office and from home.
- Interested candidates are invited to follow the link and submit a one-page cover letter and a two-page CV.
- Applications without a cover letter will not be selected.
- You must upload your cover letter and CV as two separate files (Word or pdf).
- Applicants may have to complete a written test at home as part of the recruitment process, to be scheduled at a convenient time for the candidate.
- Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments to take part in a written test or interview, following shortlisting.
- This is a full-time position, but we are very much welcoming of applications from candidates who would like to work part time.

Working at ICF means applying a passion for meaningful work with intellectual rigor to help solve the leading issues of our day. We believe in collaboration, mutual respect, open communication, and opportunity for growth.
We can only solve the world's toughest challenges by building an inclusive workplace that allows everyone to thrive. Together, our employees are empowered to share their expertise and collaborate with others to achieve personal and professional goals. 
Learn more about what we do and our commitment to inclusion.

Our people at ICF are our most important asset, so we invest in them from the moment they arrive. When you join our team, you’ll have access to a vast array of benefits to help you live your life well.
We offer a hybrid working policy, which will provide you with the flexibility to collaborate in the office, as well as in the comfort of your own home, ensuring you are able to successfully deliver the requirements of your role.
To support you, our employee wellbeing hub is designed to provide highly personalised support across a comprehensive range of wellbeing issues, such as mind, body, finances, community, career programs and HR support.

These can be spent on a large variety of high-quality items, as well as online or high-street vouchers, all with zero tax payable by the employee.
ICF also offers a range of competitive benefits, which include:

jd_text:
The Senior Consultant – Nature and Environment will support the delivery and growth of ICF’s portfolio of work for Defra and its arm’s-length bodies, with a particular focus on natural environment policy. The role is designed for someone who can combine strong project management with relevant technical, research and policy expertise. The postholder will manage multiple projects, contribute directly to technical delivery, and support the mobilisation of new work across biodiversity, nature recovery, protected sites and related environmental policy areas.
Key responsibilities
Technical delivery – nature and environment
- Contribute technical expertise to monitoring, evaluation, research and learning projects in the natural environment field.
- Support the design of evaluation questions, theories of change, monitoring frameworks, research methods and evidence synthesis approaches.
- Undertake and oversee qualitative and quantitative research, analysis and reporting, ensuring outputs are robust, practical and accessible to policy audiences.
- Apply knowledge of UK environmental policy and delivery contexts to interpret evidence and develop useful conclusions and recommendations.
- Provide technical review and quality assurance for the work of junior colleagues and delivery partners.
Project and delivery management
- Manage a portfolio of small and medium-sized nature- and environment-related projects, taking responsibility for delivery planning, resourcing, budgets, risks, quality and client reporting.
- Mobilise new projects quickly, establishing proportionate governance, clear roles, realistic workplans and effective project controls.
- Coordinate multidisciplinary ICF teams and delivery partners, ensuring inputs are integrated and deadlines are met.
- Monitor progress, dependencies, risks and financial performance, taking timely corrective action where required.
- Maintain clear and constructive client relationships, provide concise progress updates and manage changes to scope or delivery expectations
Business development and portfolio support
- Contribute to project plans and bids, including shaping methods, workplans, resourcing and budgets.
- Work flexibly across ICF’s environment portfolio, supporting priority projects and emerging client needs.
- Help identify opportunities to retain and grow nature and environment work within ICF.
- Support the development of reusable methods, tools, guidance and learning across the team.
- Coach junior staff, supporting their technical and project delivery development.
Qualifications and experience
- Degree or equivalent professional experience in environmental policy, ecology, environmental science, social research, evaluation, economics or a related discipline.
- Relevant consulting, research, policy or programme delivery experience, with demonstrable responsibility for managing projects or substantial workstreams.
- Knowledge of UK natural environment policy and delivery, such as biodiversity, nature recovery, protected sites, land management or environmental monitoring.
- Experience of monitoring, evaluation, applied research or evidence-based policy work.
- Strong project management skills, including planning, resourcing, risk management, budget oversight and quality assurance.
- Ability to contribute technically while maintaining oversight of delivery, commercial performance and client requirements.
- Strong analytical, written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear client-ready outputs.
- Experience working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external partners.
Desirable experience
- Experience delivering work for Defra, its arm’s-length bodies or other UK public-sector clients.
- Experience of theory-based, process, impact or value-for-money evaluation.
- Knowledge of biodiversity targets, nature recovery, protected sites or place-based environmental delivery.
- Experience managing supplier or partner inputs within a consultancy delivery model.
- Experience contributing to competitive proposals and developing costed workplans.
Personal qualities
- Delivery-focused, organised and able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced consulting environment.
- Collaborative and pragmatic, with the judgement to know when to resolve issues directly and when to escalate.
- Confident working with multidisciplinary teams, clients and delivery partners.
- Committed to quality, inclusion, learning and continuous improvement.
Additional points
- The role is expected to combine project management with substantive technical contribution; it is not a dedicated non-technical PM position.
- The postholder may work across several thematic areas and projects, depending on demand and subject-matter fit.
- The role will support both secured delivery and the development and mobilisation of new work.

ERM is seeking a motivated EHS Consultant who is interested in paticipating a variety of projects covering the full spectrum of ERM’s services.

Responsibilities
- Serve as the site EHS focal point, coordinating daily with the client, EPCC contractor, subcontractors and site teams.
- Monitor compliance with applicable Malaysian EHS legislation, project approvals, permit conditions, contractual requirements and approved EHS plans and procedures.
- Conduct routine inspections, joint walkthroughs and scheduled audits across construction areas, worker facilities, equipment, material storage and environmental controls.
- Verify implementation of permit-to-work systems, risk assessments, job safety analyses, toolbox meetings, competency controls, emergency arrangements and incident-reporting procedures.
- Review contractor submissions and records, including method statements, inspection reports, monitoring results, waste documentation, licences, permits, training records and statutory certificates.
- Monitor controls for high-risk activities, including work at height, lifting, excavation, confined-space entry, electrical work, hot work, traffic management, mobile plant and simultaneous operations.
- Monitor environmental controls for erosion and sediment, scheduled wastes, wastewater and effluent, dust, noise, air emissions, chemical storage, spills and sensitive receptors.
- Record observations and non-conformances, agree corrective actions with the EPCC contractor, and verify close-out within the required timeframe.
- Support incident notification, investigation and root-cause analysis, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure.
- Participate in site coordination and EHS meetings, progress reviews and emergency drills; promptly escalate significant, repeated or overdue issues to client site management.
- Prepare clear daily, weekly and monthly reports covering compliance status, inspection findings, incidents, performance indicators, outstanding actions and emerging risks.
- Liaise with regulatory authorities when authorised by the client and support inspections, submissions and follow-up actions.
- Exercise stop-work authority in accordance with project procedures where there is imminent danger, serious non-compliance or unacceptable environmental risk.
- Maintain complete, current and auditable site EHS records.
Requirements
- Degree or diploma in environmental science, engineering, occupational safety and health, construction management or a related technical discipline.
- Minimum 5 years of site-based EHS experience on construction, infrastructure, industrial or energy projects, including direct coordination with an EPCC or main contractor and subcontractors.
- Proven experience in site inspections, compliance audits, contractor-document reviews, incident investigations and corrective-action close-out.
- Strong working knowledge of Malaysian environmental and occupational safety and health legislation, licences, permits, approval conditions and construction-site compliance requirements.
- Valid Malaysian competency certification or registration relevant to the project scope, such as Safety and Health Officer, Site Safety Supervisor, a Department of Environment competent-person certification, or another recognised DOSH or DOE credential.
- Applicants must provide the certification title, issuing authority, registration or certificate number, competency scope and validity period before mobilisation.
- Practical knowledge of construction controls, including permit-to-work, risk assessment, lifting, excavation, work at height, confined spaces, hot work, traffic management and emergency response.
- Practical awareness of electrical safety, including temporary installations and distribution boards, isolation and lockout/tagout, energised-work interfaces, earthing, residual-current protection, cable management, portable tools and coordination with authorised electrical personnel.
- Practical knowledge of construction environmental controls, including scheduled wastes, wastewater, erosion and sediment, dust, noise, chemical storage and spill response.
- Ability to identify non-compliance, reference the applicable requirement and communicate practical actions to the EPCC conConfident communicator able to engage site management, supervisors, workers, contractors and regulators in English and Bahasa Malaysia.
- Ability to prepare concise site reports, meeting records and escalation notes.
- Willing and physically able to work predominantly at site, undertake frequent inspections, wear required personal protective equipment and operate safely within active construction areas.
- Valid driving licence and ability to travel to and within the project site.
- Applicants must submit a project credential sheet stating each relevant assignment’s project type, location, duration, role, EPCC or contractor interface, key responsibilities and associated competency certifications.

À propos du poste
Nous recrutons un(e) Consultant(e) Senior Eau pour développer et renforcer notre expertise en gestion de l’eau en France. Vous serez notre référent(e) sur les sujets liés à la réglementation de l’eau, à l’évaluation des risques hydriques, aux méthodologies de quantification et aux démarches de gestion durable de l’eau alignées sur les principes de l’Alliance for Water Stewardship (AWS).
Si vous maîtrisez les réglementations ICPE, les schémas SDAGE/SAGE, les questions de prélèvements et de rejets ainsi que les directives européennes relatives à l’eau, et que vous aimez accompagner les clients dans la résolution de défis concrets liés à la ressource en eau, ce poste est fait pour vous.
Vos missions
- Piloter des missions liées à l’eau : analyses réglementaires, évaluations des risques hydriques, diagnostics de sites et stratégies de gestion durable de l’eau.
- Contribuer à des propositions commerciales transversales avec les équipes CDP (risques et adaptation), LPMR (autorisations et permis) et M&A (due diligences).
- Développer un portefeuille d’activités solide dans le domaine de l’eau et renforcer le positionnement d’ERM auprès de clients stratégiques.
- Mettre à profit votre sens commercial et votre expérience auprès de clients industriels ou du secteur financier.
- Garantir l’excellence technique des missions et accompagner le développement des consultants plus juniors.
- Interagir avec aisance auprès de clients francophones ; la maîtrise du français est indispensable.
Votre profil
- 5 à 8 ans (ou plus) d’expérience en gestion de l’eau, hydrologie, réglementation de l’eau ou domaines similaires.
- Solide connaissance des cadres réglementaires français et européens liés à l’eau (ICPE, SDAGE/SAGE, Directive-cadre sur l’eau, etc.).
- Expérience des référentiels AWS ou de méthodologies de gestion durable de l’eau équivalentes.
- Excellentes compétences relationnelles et capacité à intervenir de manière autonome auprès des clients.
- Maîtrise du français et bon niveau d’anglais professionnel.
Ce que nous offrons
- Un rôle stratégique avec un impact immédiat et une forte demande de la part des clients.
- Une équipe collaborative qui valorise l’expertise, la curiosité et la bonne humeur.
- Des conditions de travail flexibles et l’opportunité de contribuer activement au développement de l’offre eau d’ERM.
- Un environnement de travail engagé en faveur de l’inclusion, de l’accessibilité et de l’égalité des chances.

We are recruiting a Senior Water Consultant to build out and elevate our water expertise in France. You will be our go‑to specialist on water regulation, water risk assessment, quantification methodologies, and AWS‑aligned stewardship.
If you can navigate ICPE, SDAGE/SAGE, withdrawals/discharges and EU directives without breaking a sweat — and you enjoy helping clients solve real‑world water challenges — this role is for you.

- Lead water‑related assignments: regulatory analysis, water risk assessments, site‑level diagnostics, stewardship strategies.
- Support cross‑service line proposals with other ERM teams covering risk & adaptation, permitting or due diligence projects
- Develop a strong water portfolio and strengthen ERM’s positioning with key clients
- Proven commercial drive and experience with industrial or financial clients.
- Ensure technical excellence and mentor junior consultants.
- Engage confidently with French‑speaking clients — fluency required.
What you can bring
- 5–8+ years of experience in water management, hydrology, water regulation, or similar fields.
- Strong understanding of French & EU water frameworks (ICPE, SDAGE/SAGE, WFD…).
- Experience with AWS or similar stewardship methodologies.
- Strong client‑facing skills and ability to deliver autonomously.
- Fluency in French and professional English.
What we Offer
- A strategic role with immediate impact and strong client demand.
- A collaborative team that values expertise, curiosity, and good humour.
- Flexible working conditions and opportunities to shape ERM’s water offering.
- A workplace committed to inclusion, accessibility, and equal opportunity.
- We encourage applications from candidates of all identities, backgrounds, and abilities.

jd_text:
ERM is the world’s largest specialist sustainability consultancy, with over 50 years of experience helping organizations navigate complex environmental, social, and governance challenges. We bring together a global community of experts to deliver meaningful impact for our clients and the planet.
Our Consulting Delivery Hub (CDH) in India is a critical part of ERM’s global consulting model enabling scalable, high-quality delivery across regions and service lines. CDH teams work in close partnership with regional consultants to support global client projects, providing specialist expertise, driving consistency, and enhancing delivery efficiency across our most important programmes.
As part of the Consulting Delivery Hub, you will collaborate with colleagues worldwide, contribute to complex sustainability projects, and play a key role in shaping the future of global consulting delivery.
Why this role matters?
As a Socioeconomic Consultant, you will support ERM’s global Impact Assessment teams by contributing social and human rights expertise to environmental and social assessments across a range of sectors and geographies. Working within the Capital Project Delivery Impact Assessment capability, you will help project teams identify social risks and impacts, apply international standards, and develop robust, practical recommendations for clients. This role is critical to ensuring the quality, consistency, and efficiency of social and human rights inputs across ERM’s global project portfolio.
What your impact is?
- Support the preparation of social and human rights inputs for environmental and social impact assessments, human rights assessments, due diligence reviews, and management plans.
- Contribute to the review and analysis of project documentation against international standards, including IFC Performance Standards, EBRD Performance Requirements, Equator Principles, and other relevant good international industry practice.
- Assist project teams in identifying social risks, human rights considerations, stakeholder engagement needs, and mitigation measures across different sectors and geographies.
- Help prepare clear, well-structured deliverables, including baseline summaries, impact assessment sections, stakeholder engagement materials, and action plans.
- Support consistent and efficient delivery across regions by working closely with senior consultants and technical specialists.
- Contribute to high-quality client outputs by applying strong research, analytical, writing, and organizational skills.
What will you bring?
- Academic background in social sciences, human rights, international development, sustainability, environmental/social management, law, political science, anthropology, sociology, or a related field.
- Initial experience or strong interest in social performance, human rights, impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, or responsible business practices.
- Understanding of international standards and frameworks relevant to social and human rights matters, such as IFC Performance Standards, EBRD Performance Requirements, Equator Principles, UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, and/or OECD guidance.
- Strong research, analytical, and written communication skills, with the ability to summarize complex information clearly and accurately.
- Ability to support multiple workstreams, manage priorities, and deliver quality outputs within agreed deadlines.
- Strong attention to detail and willingness to learn from senior technical specialists.
- Ability to work effectively with international and cross-functional teams.
- Ability to travel to project sites in remote locations.
- Fluency in English, plus French, Italian, or Spanish. Priority will be given to candidates with French and/or Italian language skills.
Preferred skills & competencies
- Exposure to international development finance institutions, lender requirements, or sustainability advisory work.
- Familiarity with labour and working conditions, community health and safety, land acquisition, indigenous peoples, cultural heritage.
- Experience working in consulting, international organizations, or development agencies.
- Ability to work in additional languages relevant to ERM’s international project portfolio.
Key responsibilities
- Support senior consultants in preparing social and human rights deliverables for international client projects.
- Conduct desk-based research, document reviews, and gap analyses against applicable international standards and client requirements.
- Assist in drafting sections of social and human rights assessments, stakeholder engagement plans, management plans, corrective action plans, and related technical outputs.
- Contribute to the identification of social risks, human rights impacts, affected stakeholders, vulnerable groups, and appropriate mitigation or management measures.
- Support the preparation of project materials, including interview guides, stakeholder mapping tools, meeting notes, data summaries, and presentation materials.
- Help maintain consistency, quality, and traceability across project documentation and deliverables.
- Collaborate with regional consultants, technical specialists, and CDH colleagues to support timely and efficient project delivery.
- Participate in internal learning, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement activities related to social performance and human rights consulting.

jd_text:
ERM is the world’s largest specialist sustainability consultancy, with over 50 years of experience helping organizations navigate complex environmental, social, and governance challenges. We bring together a global community of experts to deliver meaningful impact for our clients and the planet.
Our Consulting Delivery Hub (CDH) in India is a critical part of ERM’s global consulting model enabling scalable, high-quality delivery across regions and service lines. CDH teams work in close partnership with regional consultants to support global client projects, providing specialist expertise, driving consistency, and enhancing delivery efficiency across our most important programmes.
As part of the Consulting Delivery Hub, you will collaborate with colleagues worldwide, contribute to complex sustainability projects, and play a key role in shaping the future of global consulting delivery.
Why this role matters?
As a Socioeconomic Consultant, you will support ERM's global Capital Project Delivery (CPD) work by leading discrete socio-economic workstreams and producing high-quality analysis, impact assessment and social value inputs to major infrastructure, energy, mining and transition projects. You will work within the Social Sustainability sub‑team, partnering with regional consultants across NEBU and EMEA — including Impact Assessment, Stakeholder Engagement, Sustainable Finance, Human Rights and Political Risk leads — to deliver defensible socio-economic baselines, impact assessments and mitigation frameworks that de-risk projects and maximise positive community outcomes. This role is critical to scaling ERM's socio-economic delivery capacity, supporting CPD projects to secure consents, achieve social licence to operate, and meet growing lender, regulator and community expectations for robust socio-economic evidence.
What your impact is?
- Support socio-economic baselines and impact assessment chapters.
- Lead economic appraisal, quantification of jobs and GVA effects, and social value analysis to strengthen client business cases, funding bids and consent applications.
- Manage discrete workstreams and small project teams (1–2 people), coordinating CDH and regional inputs to deliver on time, on budget and to quality.
- Act as a trusted day-to-day point of contact for clients on socio-economic workstreams, presenting findings clearly and responding to client and regulator queries.
- Contribute socio-economic evidence across CPD sectors.
- Support bids, proposals and thought leadership.
What will you bring?
- Bachelor's degree in economics, human geography, sociology, planning, public policy, development studies or a closely related social science discipline; a master's is desirable.
- 2–3 years' relevant experience in consulting, research or policy, with a demonstrable track record of delivering socio-economic analysis, impact assessment or economic appraisal outputs.
- Proven ability to independently draft socio-economic baseline and impact assessment chapters for EIA/ESIA, or comparable economic appraisal / business case outputs.
- Sound working knowledge of UK/Irish EIA and consenting regimes (e.g. DCO, Section 36, TCPA, Planning (Wales) Act) and/or international frameworks such as the IFC Performance Standards and Equator Principles.
- Strong quantitative and qualitative research skills, including confident use of Census, ONS/NRS/NISRA/CSO, Nomis, BRES, ASHE and IMD datasets, and application of HM Treasury Green Book principles to economic.
- Experience managing discrete workstreams or small teams, including planning, budgeting, quality review and client liaison.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex socio-economic evidence into clear outputs for regulators, clients and communities.
- Strong commercial awareness and ability to work efficiently within scope, budget and time constraints.
Preferred skills & competencies
- Experience delivering socio-economic chapters for NSIPs, DCOs or comparable major infrastructure consenting regimes, or ESIA socio-economics chapters aligned with IFC PS/Equator Principles.
- Exposure to Social Impact Assessment, social value, community benefits, just transition or deliberative engagement approaches.
- Experience working in a global delivery, shared service or hub environment across time zones.
- Familiarity with automation, AI-enabled tools or GIS to support socio-economic analysis and reporting.
Key responsibilities
- Lead the preparation of socio-economic baselines drawing on Census, labour market, deprivation, housing, health, tourism and industry datasets at national, regional, local and neighbourhood scales.
- Identify and assess likely significant socio-economic effects (employment, GVA, population and demographic change, housing, community infrastructure, tourism and recreation, sociocultural effects, sense of place) across construction, operation and decommissioning phases.
- Apply and, where appropriate, refine assessment methodologies covering sensitivity/magnitude, mitigation hierarchy, cumulative effects and distributional impacts.
- Draft scoping reports, EIA/ESIA socio-economic chapters, standalone Socio-economic Statements (SES), technical notes, and inputs to ESMPs, Livelihood Restoration Frameworks and community benefit strategies.
- Deliver quantitative economic modelling of direct, indirect and induced jobs and GVA, and qualitative assessment of wider socio-economic, sociocultural and tourism effects.
- Support stakeholder mapping and engagement and integrate stakeholder feedback into socio-economic scoping and assessment.
- Manage discrete workstreams end-to-end — including scoping, planning, delivery, quality review and client communication — and coordinate CDH inputs with regional teams.
- Contribute to bids, proposals and internal capability building, including standardising templates, tools and methodologies.
- Maintain current knowledge of UK, Irish and international socio-economic policy and guidance (e.g. ISEP SIA guidance, IFC PS, HM Treasury Green Book, Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act, NPF4).
- Adhere to ERM's Health & Safety, ethics and quality management systems in all project work.

Why this role matters?
As a Wind Resource & Energy Yield Specialist, you will contribute to ERM's global renewable energy consulting practice by delivering high-quality wind resource assessments, energy yield assessments, and technical advisory services. Working within the Technical Due Diligence team, you will support wind energy projects throughout the project lifecycle, including site screening, development, financing, acquisition, construction, and operations. You will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across North America and EMEA to help clients evaluate project performance, understand technical risks, and make informed investment decisions.
What your impact is?
- Deliver bankable wind resource and energy yield assessments for utility-scale wind projects.
- Support technical due diligence assignments for project financing, mergers and acquisitions, and portfolio evaluations.
- Develop and optimize wind turbine layouts to maximize energy production while considering environmental, engineering, and permitting constraints.
- Analyze meteorological data and operational performance data to determine energy yield and identify risks and opportunities with project energyine energy yield and identify risks and opportunities with project energy yield performance.
- Provide inputs as needed for design, environmental studies, and project economics.
- Contribute to the continuous improvement of ERM's energy yield methodologies, tools, and best practices.
What will you bring?
- A solid academic background in atmospheric sciences or related engineering field (Meteorology, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering).
- Minimum 5 years of technical consulting, engineering, or operational experience during your career within the energy / infrastructure sectors.
- Strong technical skills and analytical skills.
- Experience performing wind data quality control, validation, and meteorological data analysis.
- Familiarity with Measure-Correlate-Predict (MCP) methodologies and long-term resource correction techniques.
- Understanding of wind farm loss calculations including wake losses, electrical losses, turbine performance, environmental losses, and availability assumptions.
- Familiarity with uncertainty assessments and P50/P75/P90 energy production estimates.
- Knowledge of industry standards such as IEC 61400-15 and wind resource assessment best practices. 
- Experience working with met mast, lidar, and reanalysis datasets.
Preferred qualifications, skills & competencies
- Experience preparing lender's technical advisor or independent engineer style energy yield assessments.
- Experience supporting project financing, acquisitions, or technical due diligence activities.
- Knowledge of both onshore and offshore wind resource assessments.
- Familiarity with CFD-based flow modelling and mesoscale-to-microscale wind resource modelling approaches.
- Experience analysing operational wind farm performance and SCADA datasets.
- Working knowledge of solar energy yield assessment methodologies.
- Python programming and workflow automation experience.
Key responsibilities
- Prepare technical reports, client presentations, and due diligence deliverables.
- Support proposal development through scope preparation, effort estimation, and technical inputs.
- Participate in client meetings and respond to technical questions.
- Review and QA/QC technical analyses and deliverables.
- Evaluate technical risks and opportunities associated with wind projects, including resource uncertainty, technology selection, operational performance, and project bankability.
- Collaborate with global teams and subject matter experts to deliver high-quality project outcomes.
- Contribute to methodology development, automation initiatives, and process improvements.
- Support the training and development of junior analysts where appropriate.

Your expertise will help businesses reimagine models, enhance operational performance, and create long-term value without compromising commercial goals. With ERM scaling its impact regionally, this is your opportunity to influence decision-makers and shape a future where sustainability drives growth and resilience.
Key Responsibility:

Qualifications:
- Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, or related fields.
- Minimum 3 years of professional experience in Sustainability, Climate Change, or ESG-related project.

- Proficiency in MS Office Suite: Excel, Word, and PowerPoint
- Strong project coordination and organizational skills.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Agile, adaptable, and able to work in a fast-paced consulting environment.
- Demonstrated ability to use AI tools effectively to support research, analysis, content development, and problem-solving.
- Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to evaluate, validate, and refine AI-generated outputs before applying them in professional work.
- Curious and proactive in adopting emerging digital technologies, including AI, to improve consulting effectiveness and deliver greater value to clients.
- Strong analytical and assessment skills

You will help deliver high-quality work that drives impactful programs for our clients, while building strong relationships and contributing fresh ideas to evolve our services. We offer a career path and training that supports both your technical and consulting development. Our public and private sector clients operate across a range of industries and stakeholders that present significant environmental and social sustainability issues and opportunities.
The role provides the opportunity to work with the world’s leading organisations to help solve some of the most challenging sustainability issues that our clients face globally.
Some of our clients operate in fields such as Renewable Energy, Resources, Chemicals, Power, and Technology. Many face challenges as they look to reduce their GHG emissions, manage risks posed by climate change and move towards a circular economy.
We as an organisation support our clients with facing their challenges as they look to optimise their environmental, safety and social performance, while also maximising positive impact and navigating societal and economic sustainability challenges.
We help organisations with climate change and sustainability strategy, including climate risk assessment, scenario analysis and resilience strategy.  We also support them in deriving meaning from complex datasets, including carbon emissions, to support compliance and strategic priorities.
If you are motivated and up for the challenge, we have vacancies in our Melbourne office.
Our Corporate Sustainability & Climate Change teams are looking for candidates who have interest in the following topics:
- Carbon emissions accounting, analytics and reporting
- Climate risk, resilience and adaptation
- Mandatory climate disclosures (e.g., AASB S2)
A career at ERM will provide you with:
- An entrepreneurial and performance driven culture; allowing you the ability to craft your future career.
- Immediate opportunities to work on large, complex, long-term projects which make impacts at the local, national, and global levels.
- Engagement with a strong global technical network enabling you to work and learn alongside leading industry professionals.
- A company with a solid reputation and strong client focus, working with clients in emerging and established markets creating sustainable plans to deliver growth.
Your first 12 months as an entry level employee will include:
- Access to a buddy who will guide you through life at ERM and support your development and career aspirations.
- Comprehensive onboarding program to ensure you have all the tools to hit the ground running as a consultant at ERM.
- Core consulting skills training (face-to-face and e-learning) to build your key capabilities.
- Getting straight to work – access to exciting projects and clients to put your skill into action!
Some key attributes for success:
- Relevant tertiary education in climate or environmental science
- Experience in (or demonstrated interest in) Australian climate policy and regulations through coursework, internships, research, or applied projects.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, with the ability to quickly get across new systems.
- Ability to multi-task, handling multiple project assignments with strict deadlines.
- Demonstrated analytical skills with excellent written and verbal communication.
- Ability to understand complex numerical information and use it to tell a story in reports. 
- Strong motivation and willingness to be flexible across different technical disciplines.
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
- Ability to confidently engage and consult with internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong commitment to safety; ability to follow established health and safety protocols.
Highly desirable
- Prior consulting experience
- Experience with data visualisation tools (eg. PowerBI)
- Experience in Python or R
- Experience in GIS mapping tools
- Knowledge of climate risk assessments (physical and transition risks) and scenario analysis
- Familiarity with emissions accounting and modelling, including Australian emissions regulations/process (e.g. National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting (NGER) or Greenhouse Gas Protocol)
If you are interested in an outstanding opportunity to join ERM, please apply to this Job Advert where you will be asked to complete a short application form. 
We look forward to receiving your application!

- Build and grow the Marsh HR Academy and Learning Solutions business across public workshops and in-house learning offerings

- More than 10 years of HR consulting experience across learning and development, workforce transformation, talent management, assessments, organisational development, skills and capabilities, employee experience or culture
- Well-developed problem-solving skills and the ability to shape solutions around client needs
- Ability to engage effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels
- Well-developed analytical, project management and communication skills
- High attention to detail and the ability to manage changing priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint
What makes you stand out:
- A strong network of senior HR and business relationships
- Experience in learning solutions, workforce transformation or talent consulting
- A collaborative approach and the ability to work across multiple teams and stakeholders
Why join our team:
- We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders
- We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities

Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. We are looking for a colleague to come and support our team! Do you have a sales focus/mindset, are you interested in compensation, benefits and employment practices and related software? Would you like to join an energized international team? Then this might be the role for you!
The team
The Work & Rewards Business in WTW consists of three practices: Rewards Data and Intelligence (RDI), Executive Compensation & Board Advisory (ECBA) and Work, Rewards & Careers (WRC). RDI helps companies build a competitive compensation plan by conducting annual global industry sector surveys. ECBA is focused on the way in which companies can achieve their strategic objectives through their executives. The WRC practice is dedicated to effectively design, deliver and execute employee reward strategies and programs that lead to a significant business value for our clients.
The WTW Rewards Data Intelligence Practice provides insight and advice to a large and diversified portfolio of clients that are headquartered mainly in Belgium, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the Nordic countries (we are organized as a multinational cluster). In addition, we partner with colleagues across the world daily to support our global and multinational clients. In our team, you will experience an international, diverse and inclusive environment, characterized by high energy and our professional excellence values. We offer you a very steep learning curve, and we expect you to create and grab opportunities whenever they arise.
The Role
As Business Development Manager, you will be focused on further growing the business, managing relationships with clients and selling our B2B services and products. You will be selling products which include remuneration data, compensation software and will be partnering with clients to work on broader rewards-related projects.
Further responsibilities include:
- Contribute to new business development by raising client awareness of products and services and identify cross selling opportunities.
- Develop trusted client relationships by ensuring high quality consulting advice and service is delivered. 
- Advise and consult with companies on their rewards practice and broader HR challenges.
- Provide and sell up-to-date insights, industry and market focused benchmark reports.
- Roll out a wide variety of compensation surveys and commercial activities.
- Coach people within the team.
- Building strong relationships internally and collaborate effectively with colleagues in Europe.
Requirements:
- You have at least 4 years of relevant working experience in HR or consultancy or recruiting or corporate B2B sales of products and/or services.
- You are interested in discovering the consulting environment and can’t wait to work with multiple clients across the world in a fast paced and commercial environment.
- Strong interest in HR / Compensation & Benefits with a sales mindset
- Ability to be a self-starter, initiative-taker, work independently, but also cooperatively in a team environment.
- You have strong written and verbal communication skills.
- You have excellent analytical skills, are accurate and have attention to details.
- You are proactive, flexible and have a can-do mentality.
- Fluency in English is required.

title: (Senior) Consultant (m/w/d)  Work & Rewards - Executive Compensation & Board Advisory
summary:
Für diese Einheit suchen wir ab sofort für die Standorte Frankfurt am Main / Köln / München eine(n)
Mitwirkung an nationalen und internationalen Beratungsprojekten zur Vorstands-, Geschäftsführungs- und Aufsichtsratsvergütung
Entwicklung und Weiterentwicklung von Vergütungsstrategien und Vergütungssystemen unter Berücksichtigung von Unternehmensstrategie, Kapitalmarktanforderungen, regulatorischen Vorgaben und Corporate Governance
jd_text:
Gemeinsam machen wir Potenziale produktiv. 
Im Bereich Executive Compensation & Board Advisory (ECBA) beraten wir Unternehmen, Aufsichtsräte und Vorstände bei der Gestaltung wirksamer, marktgerechter und regulatorisch belastbarer Vergütungssysteme. Wir verbinden fundierte Datenanalysen mit strategischer Vergütungsberatung und Corporate-Governance-Expertise. So unterstützen wir unsere Kunden dabei, Vergütung konsequent an Unternehmensstrategie, nachhaltiger Wertentwicklung und den Erwartungen relevanter Stakeholder auszurichten.
Für diese Einheit suchen wir ab sofort für die Standorte Frankfurt am Main / Köln / München eine(n) 
(Senior) Consultant (m/w/d) Work & Rewards - Executive Compensation & Board Advisory
Was erwartet Dich?
- Mitwirkung an nationalen und internationalen Beratungsprojekten zur Vorstands-, Geschäftsführungs- und Aufsichtsratsvergütung
- Entwicklung und Weiterentwicklung von Vergütungsstrategien und Vergütungssystemen unter Berücksichtigung von Unternehmensstrategie, Kapitalmarktanforderungen, regulatorischen Vorgaben und Corporate Governance
- Durchführung von Vergütungsbenchmarks, Peer-Group-Analysen sowie Markt- und Best-Practice-Studien
- Analyse, Design und Implementierung von Vergütungsmodellen einschließlich Grundvergütung, Short-Term Incentives, Long-Term Incentives
- Unterstützung von Aufsichtsräten und Vergütungsausschüssen bei der Überprüfung und Weiterentwicklung bestehender Vergütungssysteme
- Mitarbeit an Fachgutachten zu vergütungsbezogenen Fragestellungen, beispielsweise zur Angemessenheit und Marktüblichkeit von Vorstandsvergütung
- Erstellung von Entscheidungsvorlagen, Präsentationen und Berichten für Vorstände, Aufsichtsräte und weitere Stakeholder
- Beobachtung regulatorischer Entwicklungen sowie aktueller Trends in den Bereichen Executive Compensation, ESG und Corporate Governance
- Zusammenarbeit mit Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus unserem internationalen Executive Compensation & Board Advisory Netzwerk
Was bringst Du mit?
- Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium, vorzugsweise in Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Rechtswissenschaften, Finance, Personalmanagement oder einem vergleichbaren Studiengang
- Erste relevante Berufserfahrung bzw. für die Senior-Consultant-Rolle mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Unternehmensberatung, Executive Compensation, Corporate Governance, Human Resources, Finance oder einem vergleichbaren Umfeld
- Ausgeprägte analytische Fähigkeiten sowie Freude am Umgang mit Zahlen und komplexen Datensätzen
- Interesse an Vergütungsthemen auf Vorstands- und Führungskräfteebene sowie an Corporate-Governance-Fragestellungen
- Sicheres Auftreten und die Fähigkeit, komplexe Inhalte verständlich und adressatengerecht aufzubereiten
- Sehr gute Kenntnisse in Microsoft Excel und PowerPoint
- Hohe Kundenorientierung, Eigeninitiative und Teamfähigkeit
- Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
Neben unserem attraktiven Vergütungspaket bieten wir: 
- Work-Life-Balance – Mobiles Arbeiten oder im Büro? Flexible Arbeitszeiten? Klar, kein Problem. Wir entscheiden gemeinsam im Team, wann und wo wir arbeiten. Teammeetings und gemeinsame Brainstormings vor Ort kommen trotzdem nicht zu kurz. Hybrides Arbeiten ist bei uns mehr als ein Buzzword. 
- Attraktive Vergütung & Vorsorge – Ein attraktives,leistungsgerechtes Vergütungssysteminklusive arbeitgeberfinanzierterbetrieblicher Altersversorgung,Absicherung bei Berufsunfähigkeit sowie 30 Tage Urlaub bei Vollzeit. 
- Mobiles Arbeiten aus dem europäischen Ausland – Die Möglichkeit, bis zu 30 Tage am Stück innerhalb von 12 Monaten aus dem europäischen Ausland zu arbeiten. 
- Familienfreundlich – Wir unterstützen unsere Mitarbeitenden und ihre Familien mit einem flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodell. Neben Gleit- und Abbautagen bieten wir 5 arbeitgeberfinanzierte Kinderkranktage. 
- Freistellungen – Wir bieten eine temporäre Vollfreistellung über 2 bis 6Monate (Sabbatical),Vorruhestandsregelungen sowieSonderurlaubstage. 
- Gesundheit & Wellbeing – Mit unserem Employee Assistance Program (EAP) unterstützen wir Mitarbeitende und ihre Familien bei beruflichen und privaten Herausforderungen. Ergänztwird dieses Angebot durch Gesundheitsaktionen, Vorsorgeangeboteund einen Zuschuss zur Bildschirmarbeitsplatzbrille. 
- Firmenrad – Ein Fahrradleasing über die Entgeltumwandlung. 
- Internationalität – Eine internationale Unternehmensberatung und die Sicherheit eines globalen Konzerns mit renommierten Kunden, vom DAX-Konzern bis zum weltbekannten Mittelständler.
- Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten – Einesteile Lernkurve sowie ausreichend Freiraum für die individuelle Karriereentwicklung: Du wirst in vielfältige Themen tief eintauchen, sowohl on-the-job als auch in intensiven Fachtrainings.
Interessiert?
Wir freuen uns über Deine Online-Bewerbung. Die Bewerbung über unser Karriereportal dauert nur ca. 5 Minuten. 
WTW is an equal opportunity employer.
WTW (Willis Towers Watson) gehört zu den weltweit führenden Unternehmen in den Bereichen Advisory, Broking und Solutions. Wir unterstützen unsere Kunden dabei, aus Risiken Wachstum zu generieren. WTW ist in mehr als 140 Ländern vertreten mit 45000 MitarbeiterInnen weltweit, davon ca. 1500 im deutschsprachigen Raum an 14 Standorten in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz. Erfahre mehr über uns auf www.wtwco.de.

jd_text:
Join WTW, a global leader in talent, risk, and capital solutions. We collaborate with clients to drive effective business strategies and enhance organizational performance through our integrated approach to Work, Rewards, and Careers.
With 48,000 colleagues in over 140 countries, we help organisations make forward-thinking choices about their people, their investments and the risks they face. Joining our Executive Compensation and Board Advisory (ECBA) business, you’ll be part of this impact right from the start.
In ECBA, we provide strategic and research-driven consulting to help companies balance talent and governance risks and drive business results. Working with management and boards, we help them to balance the interest of key stakeholders and reach executive pay arrangements that stand up to scrutiny from shareholders, regulators and others. This is complex, sensitive and fascinating work. You’ll help us to deliver it to companies across a wide range of industries through a combination of expert advice, market-leading data and digital tools. So come and start building your future with a global market leader.
Curious to learn more about Work & Rewards at WTW? Discover how our unique blend of advisory expertise, data-driven insights and digital capabilities helps organisations attract, reward and engage their people.
https://careers.wtwco.com/work-and-rewards
The Role
As an Analyst you will be making an immediate and valuable contribution to a range of cross-industry client assignments. Working with market-leading data, digital tools and GenAI, and learning from experienced consultants
- Develop your consulting, practical and technical skills on our 9-month FAST START training programme
- Use your creativity and analytical skills to turn data into meaningful conclusions and insights
- Draft reports and exhibits that incorporate impactful data visualisation and storytelling for clients
- Gain exposure to real client assignments, with opportunities to begin building relationships with high-profile clients across a range of sectors
- Assist clients with drafting their Directors’ Remuneration Report - a key part of their Annual Report
- Broaden your understanding of our client solutions and the digital platforms and AI applications that are reshaping our industry
- Continuously develop your skills in the areas that align with your talents and interests
The work we do in ECBA is challenging and hugely varied. You’ll make an important contribution to data-led projects such as:
- Reviewing executive pay design to ensure pay programmes are competitive 
- Supporting clients with corporate governance, regulatory reviews and trends updates
- Providing market benchmarking on pay elements, including base pay, incentive plans and total reward
- Supporting Boards to make informed and strategic remuneration decisions
- Conducting financial analysis to support remuneration decisions and outcomes, to align pay with the performance of the company and the wider stakeholder experience
- Using data analytics, regulatory research and financial trends to help companies understand and qualify their compensation strategies
What you'll bring:
- A natural problem solver with a sharp and analytical mind
- Comfortable working with and analysing data to draw meaningful conclusions
- A confident communicator who knows how to build relationships and collaborate effectively
- Familiar, at a basic level, with using GenAI platforms to boost productivity and quality of tasks
- An active listener who can understand and respond to the needs of others
- Curious and eager to learn new skills and apply them to the ever-changing needs of our clients
- Committed to quality, continuously working to achieve the highest excellence standards
- Bachelors or Masters degree in economics, finance, mathematics, statistics or any other major with significant quantitative course work, and a strong academic record
Why Join Us?
- Make a meaningful impact in a global market leader with opportunities for professional growth.
- Work in a dynamic and multinational team across Europe.
- Be part of an organization committed to fostering diversity and an inclusive work environment.
What we offer 
Enjoy a benefits package designed to help you thrive, both professionally and personally. You'll receive 25 days of annual leave plus an extra WTW day to relax and recharge. Our comprehensive health and wellbeing offering includes private healthcare, life insurance, group income protection, and regular health assessments, all giving you peace of mind. Secure your future with our defined contribution pension scheme, featuring matched contributions up to 10% from the company.
We support your growth and balance with hybrid working options, access to an employee assistance programme, and a fully paid volunteer day to make a difference in your community. On top of these, you can opt into a variety of additional perks including an electric vehicle car scheme, share scheme, cycle-to-work programme, dental and optical cover, critical illness protection, and much more. Start making the most of your career and wellbeing with a range of benefits tailored for you.
Equal Opportunity Employer
We’re committed to equal employment opportunity and provide application, interview and workplace adjustments and accommodations to all applicants. If you foresee any barriers, from the application process through to joining WTW, please email candidatehelpdesk@wtwco.com

Our recommendations and solutions are based on rigorous research and analysis underpinned by deep expertise and thought leadership.    
What You’ll Do 
- Develop and apply advanced statistical models that help clients understand dynamic business issues. 
- Leverage analytic techniques to use data to guide client and ZS team decision-making. 
- Design custom analyses in R, Tableau, SAS, Visual Basic and Excel to investigate and inform client needs.

- Create project deliverables and implement solutions. 
- Advance problem-solving skills and improve ZS’s capabilities.

- Knowledge of programming (e.g., Java/Python/R). 
- Exposure to tools/platforms (e.g., Hadoop eco system and database systems).

- Effective oral and written communication skills. 
- Empathy, adaptability, and emotional intelligence. 
- Strong attention to detail, with a quality-focused mindset. 
- Self-discipline for planning and organizing tasks. 
- Aptitude for, and enjoyment of, working in teams.

- Collaborative spirit and problem-solving approach

ZS is seeking a Decision Analytics Associate Consultant to join the Supply Chain and Manufacturing practice, with a focus on pharmaceutical CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) drug development. This role is designed for professionals with 2–3 years of hands-on pharmaceutical experience who are ready to apply their domain expertise and quantitative modeling skills to digitalize and analytically transform CMC operations for global pharma clients. You will support project delivery, contribute to CMC data and analytics solution development, and grow your consulting skillset within a collaborative, high-impact team.

- Work collaboratively with clients to ascertain the client's specific business information needs
- Upskill on concepts relevant to solve client problems across modalities
- Execute a specific plan for analyzing the data necessary to secure solutions to clients' particular business information need(s)
- Discuss and determine with clients which specific data may be best utilized in order to perform the necessary analysis
- Evaluate, assess and analyze the data necessary to provide solutions to the client's particular business information needs
- Communicate the data results to the client, with an emphasis on answering the business question as opposed to the analytical and reporting processes used
- Gain immediate familiarity with client's internal processes
- Develop expertise within a client analytics area
- Be available for clients during regular working hours

- Support model validation, verification, and documentation aligned with Quality by Design (QbD) principles and regulatory expectations (e.g., ICH Q8/Q9/Q10)

- Advance problem-solving skills and improve ZS’s capabilities;

- Hands-on experience building/using first-principles (e.g., CFD, DEM) and AI/ML models for pharma process development for at least one modality
- Experience developing and managing production-grade codes for models, including models' lifecycle management
- Knowledge of key concepts including unit operations, processes, Quality by Design (QbD), tech transfer, process validation, quality attributes, and regulatory milestones across pharma development
- Ability to translate the knowledge of concepts in one modality to other modalities, if needed
- Understanding of the different data and information systems such as ELN, LIMS, ERP systems, and LCM or PLM systems
- Optional: Understanding of the CMC related regulatory submission requirements
- Experience presenting to senior leaders, executives, and audiences with CMC backgrounds
- Ability to lead multiple workstreams and demonstrate effective time and project management skills
- Capability to simplify complex concepts into easily understandable frameworks and presentations 
- Proficiency in working within a virtual global team environment, contributing to the timely delivery of multiple projects 
- Travel to other offices as required to collaborate with clients and internal project teams
- Fluency in English.
- Client-first mentality.

- Collaborative spirit and problem-solving approach.
